claims.label: Test configuration
claims.value: G1 EDU-4, Dex3-1 three-finger hands, firmware 1.04
claims.assessment: Fraunhofer identifies the tested configuration and states that the unit was delivered in May 2025; results should not be generalized to other variants or firmware versions without qualification.

claims.label: Energy and endurance
claims.value: 239 W mean power and 1:49 h derived per-charge endurance in the defined typical scenario
claims.assessment: Fraunhofer measures power in standardized standing and walking conditions and derives maximum operating times from those results. The 1:49 figure is not presented as an observed continuous field run or cumulative runtime. Fraunhofer also reports 154 W standing, 272 W level walking, 283 W at 10% incline and a derived 2:49 h for standing only.

sourceMetric.term: maximum operating time in the typical scenario

metricAssessment.interpretation: This is a scenario-derived energy-endurance result. It is valid for the stated laboratory scenario, but it does not measure availability against scheduled operating time.

claims.label: Walking speed
claims.value: 0.49 m/s slow and 0.84 m/s fast walking measured with 3D tracking
claims.assessment: A 3 kg load did not reduce steady walking speed in the described test, but increased acceleration and deceleration time by several tenths of a second.

claims.label: Thermal constraint
claims.value: Outstretched arms could shut down after one to two minutes without added payload
claims.assessment: Fraunhofer attributes the shutdown and dropping arms to actuator overheating. No frequency across repeated trials or recovery time is published.

claims.label: Collision force
claims.value: Mean peak forces of approximately 510 N at the chest and 530 N at the abdomen in specified walking collisions
claims.assessment: Fraunhofer's public safety guide states that displayed values are mean peak forces from at least three trials per scenario with the robot in fast mode at about 1 m/s. It does not publish the underlying observations, spread or unit-to-unit variation.

claims.label: Stability and recovery
claims.value: No balance loss on cable-channel steps or a 20% ramp; recovery depended on floor friction
claims.assessment: Self-stabilization was strong in the described tests, while standing up from the back failed on smooth tile and wood because the arms could slip.

claims.label: Cybersecurity
claims.value: Bluetooth remote-code-execution vulnerability found in the tested software state
claims.assessment: Fraunhofer reports that the vulnerability persisted across several firmware updates and was subsequently closed by a newer update.

claims.label: Delivered autonomy
claims.value: Remote-controlled walking available after delivery; further capabilities require user implementation
claims.assessment: This is the observed baseline of the tested EDU configuration, not a claim about every later software stack built on the platform.

records.finding: Fraunhofer publishes useful measurements that reveal concrete operating constraints, including scenario-based power draw, derived per-charge endurance, actuator overheating and collision force. Availability is not applicable to this bounded laboratory benchmark because it defines no scheduled operating window; the tests also do not establish field availability, failure frequency, intervention rate or repair time. The public material does not report repeat counts or uncertainty for most tests.

states.basis: Reconstructed cumulatively from all dated Fraunhofer sources available through 3 June 2026.

limitations: Laboratory measurements should not be generalized into field availability or fleet reliability.
The results apply to the identified hardware and software state.

deployment_signal.reason: A dated public source establishes a relevant program or activity, but the public result does not yet meet the full-record gate.

no_qualifying_public_result.label: No qualifying public result
no_qualifying_public_result.reason: The initial search did not find a sufficiently bounded public result for either a full record or a directory signal by the cutoff date.

sourcePreservation.publicBoundary: Public pages and exports expose the original URL, capture time, exact locator, internal artifact reference, media type, byte length and SHA-256 fingerprint, but not the captured third-party content.
sourcePreservation.rights: Artifacts are retained for internal editorial verification. HumanoidUptime claims no ownership or republication right in third-party source content.

externalReviews.invitation: Researchers, operators, engineers and other subject-matter readers can propose a scoped spot check of a named record, claim or source trail.
externalReviews.publicationRule: A completed external spot check is listed only with the reviewer's permission and shows the reviewer, scope, completion date and whether it changed the public record. A spot check does not imply endorsement of the whole dataset.
